pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

Writes to annotations are sometimes rejected on MySQL due to a recurring deadlock with the annotation cleanup job.
Details here: https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/64979

**Why do we need this feature?**

The deadlock seems to be a result of the subquery, under normal circumstances a plain insert and delete should not lock, and there are no extended transactions at play.

This PR splits the subquery into a separate SQL statement. These statements do not share a transaction, and therefore allow locks to flush in between.

Unfortunately we could not reduce this to a single DELETE statement, due to the batching - DELETE LIMIT is not supported on all databases without needing to reintroduce the subquery. The IDs loaded into memory are of bounded size due to the batch size configuration.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/64979

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [x] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [x] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-a-whats-new-document), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: Annotations: Split cleanup into separate queries and deletes to avoid deadlocks on MySQL

raw_findings.body: The generated `DELETE ... IN (...)` exceeds the driver's bind-parameter limit and cleanup fails instead of processing the configured batch. The previous single-statement implementation did not create one bind parameter per selected ID.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Supported database backends reject oversized prepared statements, causing annotation cleanup to return an error.
raw_findings.impact: The generated `DELETE ... IN (...)` exceeds the driver's bind-parameter limit and cleanup fails instead of processing the configured batch. The previous single-statement implementation did not create one bind parameter per selected ID.
raw_findings.root_cause: The refactor converts every selected ID into an individual SQL placeholder without applying a parameter-count limit except for SQLite.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Split `ids` into database-safe parameter chunks before issuing DELETE statements (or validate and cap the configured batch size per dialect), and sum the affected-row counts.
raw_findings.title: Bound DELETE bind parameters for non-SQLite databases
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator configures `annotations.cleanupjob_batchsize` above the database driver's parameter limit (for example, 65536 on PostgreSQL or over 2100 on SQL Server) and that many eligible annotation or tag IDs are selected in one batch.

finding.verifier_reason: Patch shows line 615 creates placeholders for all IDs without chunking for non-SQLite databases. Code only handles SQLite parameter limit (999). The trigger requires admin to configure large batch size AND that many IDs exist, which is realistic but requires specific configuration.
